from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Harmonic Series and Convergence", [
            "Consider the infinite series 1/n to the s.",
            "It converges precisely when s is greater than 1.",
            "Think of this like Zeno’s paradox in reverse."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        harmonic_series = MathTex(r"\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s} = 1 + \frac{1}{2^s} + \frac{1}{3^s} + \dots", font_size=36)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(harmonic_series, "B2")))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00BFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")
        condition = Text("s > 1", color="#32CD32", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(condition, "D3")
        self.play(FadeIn(condition))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00BFFF")
        
        # Simple representation of Zeno-like steps
        steps = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.3, color=WHITE).shift(i*0.4*RIGHT) for i in range(5)])
        self.place_at_grid(steps, "F2")
        self.play(Create(steps))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Riemann Zeta Function", [
            "We define the Riemann Zeta function as this sum.",
            "For s greater than 1, the series works perfectly.",
            "Analytic continuation extends this to the complex plane."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        zeta_formula = MathTex(r"\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(zeta_formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(zeta_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        s_text = MathTex(r"s \in \mathbb{C}, \text{Re}(s) > 1", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(s_text, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(s_text))
        
        sum_expansion = MathTex(r"1 + \frac{1}{2^s} + \frac{1}{3^s} + \dots", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_expansion, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(sum_expansion))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Create a simple representation of complex plane
        plane = ComplexPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, "E3", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(zeta_formula), FadeOut(s_text), FadeOut(sum_expansion))
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Zeta connects directly to the world of primes.",
            "The sum equals an infinite product over primes.",
            "Every integer is built from prime building blocks."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Magic Connection: Euler Product Formula", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        zeta_formula = MathTex(r"\zeta(s) = \prod_{p} \left(1 - p^{-s}\right)^{-1}", font_size=36)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(zeta_formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(zeta_formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        sum_formula = MathTex(r"\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{-s}", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_formula, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(sum_formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        blocks = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(3)])
        blocks.arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(blocks, 'E4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(blocks))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Riemann Hypothesis: The Critical Strip", [
            "The critical strip lies between 0 and 1.",
            "The hypothesis concerns where the function equals zero.",
            "All non-trivial zeros lie on line 1/2."
        ])
        
        # Complex plane grid setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False},
        ).scale(0.6)
        
        critical_strip = Rectangle(
            width=axes.c2p(1, 0)[0] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[0],
            height=axes.c2p(0, 2)[1] - axes.c2p(0, -2)[1],
            fill_opacity=0.3,
            fill_color=BLUE,
            stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(axes.c2p(0.5, 0))
        
        critical_line = Line(axes.c2p(0.5, -2), axes.c2p(0.5, 2), color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        
        # Zeros
        zeros = VGroup(*[
            Dot(axes.c2p(0.5, i * 0.5), color=YELLOW) 
            for i in range(-3, 4) if i != 0
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(critical_strip))
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(axes, critical_strip), 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(zeros))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(critical_line))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Impact", [
            "This remains mathematics' most elusive, unsolved prize.",
            "It holds the key to prime number distribution.",
            "The quest for the proof continues today."
        ])
        
        # Animation Elements
        prime_group = VGroup(
            Text("2", color=BLUE), Text("3", color=BLUE), Text("5", color=BLUE),
            Text("7", color=BLUE), Text("11", color=BLUE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        zeta_eq = MathTex(r"\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}", color=WHITE)
        lock = Text("🔒", font_size=72)
        library_bg = Rectangle(width=4, height=4, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.place_in_area(library_bg, 'B2', 'E5')
        self.play(FadeIn(library_bg))
        self.place_at_grid(lock, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(lock))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(zeta_eq, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(prime_group, 'E4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(zeta_eq), FadeIn(prime_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=96, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(question_mark, 'C4')
        self.play(FadeIn(question_mark), run_time=2)
        self.play(Indicate(lock))

outline.topic: The Riemann Zeta Function: Bridging Arithmetic and Geometry
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate STEM students with a foundation in Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Harmonic Series and Convergence
sections.content: Establish the foundation by looking at the p-series. Explain how the series 1/n^s converges only when s > 1, setting the stage for the definition of the Zeta function.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Zeno's Paradox' scenario: An ant traveling halfway to a cookie, then a quarter, then an eighth. Summing these distances converges to 1 (the cookie).

sections.title: Defining the Riemann Zeta Function
sections.content: Formally introduce ζ(s) = Σ 1/n^s. Explain that for s > 1, this is a standard sum, but for other complex values, we must use 'Analytic Continuation' to extend its domain.
sections.example: An animation showing a map expanding: starting with a small 'real' island, then drawing lines into the 'complex' ocean (the complex plane) to reveal the full landmass.

sections.title: The Magic Connection: Euler Product Formula
sections.content: Demonstrate the bridge between the Zeta function and Prime Numbers. Show the equivalence between the summation of integers and the infinite product of primes.
sections.example: A sieve visual: A machine that sorts integers into their prime 'DNA' components, demonstrating how the Zeta function acts as a filter for prime numbers.

sections.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: The Critical Strip
sections.content: Discuss the 'Critical Strip' (0 < Re(s) < 1). Introduce the Riemann Hypothesis: all non-trivial zeros lie on the line Re(s) = 1/2. Explain its significance to prime number distribution.
sections.example: A radar display: The Zeta function is represented as a wave. The zeros are 'pings' on the radar. The Hypothesis predicts they all align perfectly on a single vertical laser beam.

sections.title: Conclusion and Impact
sections.content: Summarize why this is the 'Holy Grail' of mathematics: understanding the 'music' of prime numbers. Acknowledge that a proof remains the most elusive prize in math.
sections.example: A closing shot of a giant library where the bookshelf containing the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is the only one locked, waiting for the next generation to find the key.
